product_guards: Require typed, coherent direct HTML 404 or 410 observations at the exact requested URL. Refuse missing or conflicting observations, access restrictions, rate limits, server errors, timeouts, blocked hosts and redirects ending in error. The tracked 4xx family remains broader than the deliberately repairable subset.

Require one literal sitemap in a known static directory without a sitemap generator. Reject a source binding for any missing URL in the supplied repository index, ambiguous or changed routing, wildcards, conditions and competing configurations. Reuse the existing flat-rule guard; even a configured 404/410 rule at the source is conservatively refused, rather than inferred from a serving error page.

Immediately before the single XML PUT, recheck each verified URL with GET using the existing public-target guard, without URL credentials, redirects or response body consumption, with bounded connection/read timeouts and response closure. Require the same direct 404/410, an HTML content type, exact response URL, no redirect history and no Retry-After. Any changed or unavailable witness blocks the whole write.

Reuse the validated exact XML node deletion. Preserve path case, query, slash, comments, line endings, extensions, unrelated entries and all bytes outside deleted nodes. Refuse malformed XML, DTD, indexes, ambiguous locs, oversized sources and unreadable sitemap SHA. Never create missing pages or alter routing/navigation/page files.

No inferred generator exclusion or heuristic targeting after refusal, and no free-form or cached preview bypass. Individual deep and bulk endpoints share the deterministic implementation with zero provider calls or AI billing. A new premise note requires human review even in auto mode: an observed absence does not establish the owner's intent to abandon the page.

A verified subset may be prepared with refused URLs explicitly named and the existing advisory about potential hreflang partner effects. Other sitemap families, catalog, auditor and historical validation records remain unchanged. Target resolver candidates alone do not authorize editing a generated sitemap.

seo_reference.usage: Google treats 429 as a server-overload signal, separately from other 4xx responses. Restricting this repair to observed/rechecked 404 and 410 is a conservative product choice, not a claim that every other 4xx remains indexable or that an absence is permanently intentional.

successful_live_cycle.preput_http_namespace: The bench maps only these exact controlled production-namespace URLs to their observed baseline deploy-preview host, then calls the unmodified product status probe. It never substitutes a fabricated response or contacts customer URLs.

independent_countercheck.description: Re-read main, seed, baseline and correction refs, both closed draft unmerged PRs and exact successful builds. Verify two setup commits and one corrective commit affecting only sitemap.xml. Independently parse retained XML entries without inter-entry tails and compare complete output bytes to removal of two unique fixture blocks. Verify actual served XML, current 404 responses on both previews using fresh requests and the product probe, source absence in all three trees, preserved navigation/rules and a healthy master body/canonical/preview header. Re-prepare the baseline without models, writes, file targeting or quota calls.

acceptance_inventory.after_snapshot: acceptance-after-final.json in the live temporary directory

initial_red.explanation: Repeated probes of unchecked flag-based deletion and missing HTTP revalidation, not 63 independent defects.

first_implementation_run.explanation: Three existing positive XML tests provided no page observations. Enrich their fixture with an actual typed direct HTML 404 observation and keep every deletion/preservation assertion. All new protection assertions remained unchanged.

limitations: Owned static HTML repository, unique literal XML and direct missing URLs only. Remote witnesses are two natural 404s; 410, protected/rate-limited/transient responses, source restoration and invalid probes are tested synthetically, not rebuilt on every remote platform. The family tracks other 4xx codes that are intentionally not auto-repaired.

Native previews retain their noindex policy and canonical-host alias context. XML serves production-host URLs with zero sitemap crawl seeds, so raw counts 0 to 0 establish no repair. The existing exact host/header projection with actually served XML measures 2 to 0; independent HTTP/source/XML checks prove only this bounded correction, not production indexing.

Generated, ambiguous, multi-source or computed sitemaps, non-HTML responses and missing URLs with source bindings or configured rules are conservatively refused. Delisting does not restore pages, repair inbound links or resolve multilingual partner effects. Navigation intentionally retains the two absent witnesses after delisting so disappearing observations cannot create a false success.

The HTTP probe reuses the existing public-target validator; this phase is not a complete SSRF/DNS-rebinding audit. Reads of the supplied tree, current sitemap SHA and live HTTP status are not an atomic transaction across Git, hosting and later deployment. Concurrent branch changes, later source restoration or temporary server-side absence remain possible and require human review.

No agent deployment, customer onboarding, fresh real Claude integration, production recovery replay, receipt migration, scheduler/payment acceptance, capacity test or fresh PostgreSQL run is included. SQLite retains 42 skipped tests. No all-green catalog or client-readiness certification is claimed.
next_acceptance_check: Measure HTTP URLs listed in an HTTPS site's sitemap on an owned rebuilt fixture, then remaining offered families and client onboarding.
